types.description: The learner selected the mathematically appropriate model or representation.
The learner formed a mathematically valid relation from the stated conditions.
An equation-to-equation transformation does not preserve equality.
A compound expression is silently reinterpreted as a variable or value.
A squared binomial is expanded with an invalid constant, sign, or cross term.
Evidence does not preserve or clearly distinguish x/y coordinate roles.
The slope relation reverses or inconsistently maps coordinate differences.
The learner or extractor copied source data inconsistently; this is not itself mathematical weakness.
No independent verification step is observed.
A verification attempt is performed but does not correctly test the proposed result.
A division computation is incorrect after the mathematical relation is already established.
A nearby but non-equivalent definition is substituted for the required one.
